rows.target_title: Oil Par Prices
rows.basis: The MRF Guidelines state that Alberta Energy determines a well's monthly revenue by 'multiplying volumes of all the hydrocarbons produced, including test production, by their respective par/reference prices as published in the Information Letters available on the Alberta Energy website' (Revenue = Production * Par Price), and that 'the price component of oil is determined by using the monthly oil par price (PP) based on density'. The rate brackets are literal par-price thresholds: PP <= 251.70, 251.70 < PP <= 409.02, 409.02 < PP <= 723.64, 723.64 < PP. The Petroleum Royalty Regulation, 2017 s.5 gives the Minister the power to 'determine an amount per cubic metre as the par price' for light, medium, heavy and ultra-heavy oil, and its Schedule sets rp% = [(par price - 251.70) x ...].

rows.target_title: Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price
rows.basis: Under MRF the post-C* royalty rate is rp% + rq%, where 'the price component (rp) is the percentage rate based on the par/reference price for each hydrocarbon'. C* is drawn down each month by revenue 'valued using the respective hydrocarbon par/reference price', and the gas rate tables in the guidelines are indexed on the monthly reference price in $/GJ. The Natural Gas Royalty Regulation, 2017 correspondingly requires the Minister to prescribe a Gas Reference Price 'for January, 2017 and for each subsequent' production month along with the methane, ethane, propane, butanes and pentanes plus ISC reference prices.

rows.target_title: NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil (WTI) Futures Daily Settlement Prices
rows.basis: Oil Sands Royalty Regulation, 2009 (AR 223/2008) s.29 sets the gross royalty rate as RG% = 1% + [FG (A - B)], where FG is '8% divided by $65 per barrel', A is 'the lesser of the WTI price for the given month ... and $120 per barrel' and B is 'the lesser of A for the month and $55 per barrel'. s.29(3)(a) defines the monthly WTI price as 'the simple average of the WTI prices for the trading days of the preceding month, excluding any days where the trading price was at or below $0 per barrel', and s.29(4)(a) defines the daily WTI price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of West Texas Intermediate crude futures as traded on NYMEX'. The same A term drives the post-payout net royalty percentage factor, NRPF = 25% + (FN (A - B)).

rows.target_title: Alberta Natural Gas Reference Price
rows.basis: The Fiscal Plan's Fiscal Year Assumptions table carries an 'Alberta Reference Price (Cdn$/GJ)' row beside WTI and WCS, and the footnote to that table states that 'The Alberta Reference Price (used in natural gas royalty calculations) represents the average field price of all Alberta gas sales which normally follows the Western Canada regional benchmark.' The revenue chapter then forecasts natural gas and by-product royalties off that assumption — the ARP is forecast at C$3.00/GJ in 2026-27, up from C$1.70/GJ in 2025-26, with royalties rising from $0.7 billion to $0.9 billion.

rows.target_title: Alberta Economic Outlook
rows.basis: The Fiscal Plan reports the in-year revision against the same energy price assumptions the Economic Outlook set at budget: non-renewable resource revenue is 'a $0.8 billion decrease from budget', because 'The West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price is expected to average US$61.50 per barrel (/bbl) in 2025-26, a US$6.50/bbl decrease from the Budget 2025 estimate' and 'the light-heavy differential is expected to average US$11.20/bbl for 2025-26, US$5.90/bbl narrower than budgeted'. The in-year statements exist to restate revenue against a revised version of the budget's price forecast.

candidates.sentence: Sources: The Budget Lab at Yale, Alberta Treasury Board and Finance; 2025 is updated till November Economic Outlook | Fiscal Plan 2026 – 29 23 Economic Outlook 2026-29 Heightened geopolitical risk adds to uncertainty 2026 is proving to be another volatile year for the global economy as it navigates a fragmented trade landscape and unstable geopolitical climate.

rows.target_title: AER General Well Data Report (General Well File)
rows.basis: The 2025 Alberta Linear Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines define 'AER means the Alberta Energy Regulator' and then read assessment inputs straight out of its records: for pipelines and wells licensed by the AER 'the assessment must reflect the characteristics and specifications as of October 31 of the assessment year, as contained in the records of the AER'. Pipeline assessment classification codes are set by 'pipeline material, outside diameter, and the maximum operating pressure ... as contained in the records of the AER', and well depth is taken field by field — 'Total depth (field WELL-TOTAL-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 010)', 'Deepest shoe set depth (field SHOE-SET-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 040)', plug tops from record type 055. The guidelines also rely on the AER Insolvency List.

rows.target_title: ICE Brent Crude Futures Daily Settlement Prices
rows.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(f) defines the Brent price as 'the settlement price for the day of the prompt month contract of the Brent crude futures as traded on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)'. That term enters the monthly Floor Price through A = greater of $0 and (BRENT - WTI), alongside the WTI term already recorded. Promoted from _dropped in V0.5 under the commercial-source decision: the evidence is exactly as strong as the WTI edge and was only ever held back because ICE is a commercial exchange.

rows.target_title: Argus Mexico Maya Spot Price, FOB US Gulf Coast
rows.basis: Bitumen Valuation Methodology (Ministerial) Regulation (AR 232/2008) s.1(3)(e) states that 'the daily Mexico Maya Spot Price FOB at the U.S. Gulf Coast shall be as published by Argus Media Inc.' The MMSP is the leading term in the Floor Price: Floor Price = greater of $10/m3 and MMSP - $250/m3 - A. Alberta legislation names a private price-reporting agency by company name, which is as explicit as evidence gets.

rows.target_title: System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)
rows.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (www.ibge.gov.br contas-nacionais path, plain curl, HTTP 200, 132,905 bytes — this path served genuine bytes where the PNAD Contínua path on the same host returned a WAF 403). IBGE's own page: "As informações da série do Sistema de Contas Nacionais - referência 2010, cabe ressaltar, são apresentadas segundo uma classificação de produtos e atividades integrada com a Classificação Nacional de Atividades Econômicas - CNAE 2.0 e estão em conformidade com o System of national accounts 2008, SNA 2008, manual preparado sob os auspícios da Organização das Nações Unidas - ONU, da Comissão Europeia - Eurostat, do Fundo Monetário Internacional - FMI, da Organização de Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico - OCDE e do Banco Mundial, o que reflete o compromisso do IBGE com a sistemática de revisões periódicas de suas práticas, conforme preconizam as recomendações internacionais." "Em conformidade com" is a methodology claim, not a citation for context, and the sentence names the manual, its edition and its five sponsoring bodies. Brazil's first edge into the international-standards.json layer, and the same shape the corpus already carries for Canadian, German and Antipodean national accounts. Note that sna-2008 is itself superseded by the 2025 SNA per its own node description, with country rollout targeting 2029-2030; IBGE's current rebasing exercise (reference year moving from 2010 to 2021) is the natural moment for that transition, but IBGE's page states only the rebasing, not an SNA edition change, so nothing is asserted about it here.

rows.target_title: 中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法 (财预〔2022〕58号) — Measures for Equalization Transfer Payments from the Central Government to Local Governments
rows.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and the strongest single edge found for China this round. Ningxia's own first article names the central measures by exact bracketed title: 「为加快建立现代财政制度…推进基本公共服务均等化，根据《中华人民共和国预算法》及《中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法》，特制定自治区对市县均衡性转移支付办法。」 Restated in the covering notice: 「根据《中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法》等有关规定，经报请自治区人民政府研究同意，自治区财政厅修订了…」 `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`, because the provincial instrument does not merely reference the central one -- it REPLICATES its formula: Ningxia's own 「某县标准收支缺口财力补助=（市县标准收入-市县标准支出）×补助系数」 is structurally the central 第四条's standard-expenditure-minus-standard-revenue-times-coefficient form, re-expressed one tier down. That is genuine method inheritance, the same distinction `br-ipca-fpe.json` uses to type `br-fpe-dn-tcu -> br-lc-62-1989` as `methodology_depends_on`. TENSE: 「根据 … 特制定」 is present and constitutive.

rows.target_title: 中华人民共和国预算法 (Budget Law of the People's Republic of China)
rows.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, from the same single sentence as the edge above -- Ningxia's 第一条 names both instruments together: 「…根据《中华人民共和国预算法》及《中央对地方均衡性转移支付办法》，特制定自治区对市县均衡性转移支付办法。」 `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` for the same reason as the central measures' own edge to the Budget Law: the statute establishes the transfer-payment system and its equalisation objective but supplies no calculation method. Worth recording that this makes the Budget Law's authority visible at two tiers of government from documents' own text, which is the shape this corpus exists to draw.

rows.target_title: Chartered Bank Prime Lending Rate
rows.basis: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (browser/websearch session, closing G.64.md cheap check 2). The Bank of Canada's own explainer states the mechanism: 'What's behind your mortgage rate' (bankofcanada.ca, May 27, 2020) -- 'These include the prime rate, which is used by the banks as a basis for pricing variable-rate mortgages.' Typed uses_data_from rather than calculated_from, matching this file's own boc-prime-rate -> boc-policy-rate precedent: the explainer describes a market convention (prime plus or minus a lender-set spread), not a formula stated by the published series' own methodology page, and the published aggregate is a volume-weighted average of what banks actually charged rather than a recalculation of prime itself.

The dependence is operative, not decorative: Article 1(2) defines 'Government' as 'the sector of general government (S.13)... as defined in ESA 2010', Article 1(3) defines 'Government deficit (surplus)' as 'the net borrowing (net lending) (B.9) of the sector of general government (S.13), as defined in ESA 2010', and Article 1(5) defines 'Government debt' by ESA 2010 categories 'currency and deposits (AF.2); debt securities (AF.3) and loans (AF.4)'. rows.target_title: General Consumer Price Index (CAPMAS), 10th series
rows.basis: Article 35 sets the pension increase floor directly equal to 'the rate of inflation', and the Act's own definitions section defines 'Inflation Rate' as the change in CAPMAS's General Consumer Price Index, determined every April. CAPMAS's CPI print is a direct, named input into the statutory floor of the calculation (capped at 15%), not merely referenced as context.

rows.target_title: Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y), the payroll-tax revenue base, makes SEPH a named term in a statutory formula: 'P is the gross dollar value, before deductions, of the payrolls of all employers in the province for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours, other than the payrolls of (i) employers not included in that survey, and (ii) employers in the following industry classifications, as defined by the North American Industry Classification System: (A) the elementary and secondary schools industry group, (B) the hospitals subsector, (C) the nursing and residential care facilities subsector, (D) the provincial and territorial public administration subsector, and (E) the local, municipal and regional public administration subsector'. `calculated_from` because P is a term in the formula, not a consideration — the same test that makes boc-bank-rate calculated_from the policy rate. Note the provision also carves out its own exclusions by NAICS classification, so the edge to `naics` is stated in the same sentence. SCOPE, stated because the section number alone overstates it: s. 8 sits in DIVISION 2 — Nova Scotia, and defines revenue base 'For the purpose of sections 3.71 to 3.9 of the Act', which are the Nova Scotia additional-equalization provisions. SEPH does NOT appear in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base at s. 5 — the phrase 'payrolls' occurs nowhere in ss. 1 through 8(1)(j), because the 2007 reform folded payroll taxes into the personal-income base. So this is the Equalization Program depending on SEPH through one division of the Regulations, not through the general formula.

rows.target_title: Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts
rows.basis:
MERGED 2026-08-09 (EU/G.73.md): this one edge was defined three times across two slices — twice in equalization-named-products.json and once here — so `npm run validate`'s last-wins load dropped two of the three bases silently, taking two independent statutory citations with them. All three are preserved below; the two duplicate objects were deleted from equalization-named-products.json and this object, the only one carrying a reference_period, was kept.

(a) SOR/2007-303 s. 3.1 (DIVISION 1 definitions) names the framework three times, once for each of three capital-formation aggregates: 'gross fixed capital formation in intellectual property products, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'; 'gross fixed capital formation in non-residential structures, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data for or from its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. Minted 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Q1, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx): the framework is a node in its own right, matching the statute's own wording verbatim rather than an inferred release.
[evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2007-303/page-2.html]

(b) SOR/2007-303 s. 5(b)(i), the DIVISION 1 all-provinces revenue base: 'the portion of the aggregate of corporate profits in Canada, before the payment of income taxes and without any deduction of the aggregate of corporate losses in Canada, that is attributable to any of the 10 provinces for the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. A fourth, independent citation of the framework, distinct from the three capital-formation terms in s. 3.1. Minted 2026-08-08, same ruling.
[evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2007-303/page-3.html]

(c) Two further terms of the same formula at SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(y) are pinned to the national accounts. 'A is the total wages and salaries excluding supplementary labour income, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts, paid in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, other than the wages and salaries paid by (i) the federal general government sector to employees in the defence industry, and (ii) the provincial and territorial general government sector and the local general government sector to their employees'. And 'M is military pay and allowances, excluding supplementary labour income, paid in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its System of Macroeconomic Accounts'. RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (Thomas, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx Q1): the Regulations name the *System of Macroeconomic Accounts* itself, not a specific release, and Thomas's ruling was to mint the framework as its own node rather than infer a mapping to one of its releases. Target repointed from the inferred statcan-national-accounts (IMDB record 1901, GDP by income and expenditure) to statcan-system-macroeconomic-accounts, which now matches the statutory wording verbatim rather than through a judgement call. This sidesteps, rather than resolves, the still-open statcan-hfce / statcan-national-accounts duplication question recorded in statcan-macro-accounts.json — that question is about which release-level node is authoritative and remains open on its own terms.

rows.target_title: Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold
rows.basis: Named twice as a survey by title. SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(d)(ii): 'the number of litres of aviation fuel sold in the province or territory in that year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of data from its survey Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold'. And s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(A), for railway fuel: 'in the case where railway fuel is taxed in the province or territory throughout that year and data on the tax is complete and available, by Statistics Canada on the basis of data from its survey Gasoline and Other Petroleum Fuels Sold'.

rows.target_title: Report on Energy Supply and Demand in Canada
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(e)(ii)(B), the fallback where railway fuel tax data is incomplete: 'in any other case, by the Minister on the basis of data prepared by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its publication entitled Report on Energy Supply and Demand in Canada'. rows.basis: Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'The quality report covers a number of quality indicators (completeness, revision policy and practice, punctuality, coherence and documentation on methodology), adhering to the requirements for the Single Integrated Metadata Structure, which were endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee in November 2015.' THIS EDGE IS THE SLICE'S HEADLINE: the Implementing Regulation that governs this report declines to name SIMS, calling it only 'the European Statistical System standards on quality reporting published by the Commission (Eurostat)' (recital 5), and a search of the whole instrument for 'SIMS', 'Single Integrated', 'ESMS', 'ESQRS' and 'Handbook' returns zero hits. rows.target_title: Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council on European statistics
rows.basis: Quality report on national and regional accounts, 2025 edition (KS-01-25-052), Executive summary, page 5: 'This requires the quality of national and regional accounts data sent to Eurostat to be assessed against the quality criteria set out in the Regulation on European statistics (Regulation (EC) No 223/2009).' The criteria themselves are Article 12(1): 'To guarantee the quality of results, European statistics shall be developed, produced and disseminated on the basis of uniform standards and of harmonised methods. In this respect, the following quality criteria shall apply: (a) relevance … (g) coherence', and Implementing Regulation 2016/2304's Annex §3 structures the reports around them: 'The quality reports shall include information on all the quality criteria laid down in Article 12(1) of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009. The information shall be presented according to the following structure: Relevance; Accuracy and reliability; Timeliness and punctuality; Accessibility and clarity; Coherence and comparability.' Both documents read from source 2026-08-07.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index
rows.basis: The CRA page opens: 'Each year, certain personal income tax and benefit amounts are indexed to inflation using the Consumer Price Index data as reported by Statistics Canada.' The statutory mechanism is Income Tax Act s. 117.1(1)(b)(ii), which sets the adjustment factor as (A/B) - 1 where 'A is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period that ended on September 30 next before that year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for the 12 month period immediately preceding'; s. 117.1(4) defines that index as 'the Consumer Price Index for Canada, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act' averaged over the twelve months of the period. Section 18(5) defines the term: 'The Wage Measure for a month is the average weekly wages and salaries of (a) the Industrial Aggregate in Canada for the month as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act.' rows.target_title: Provincial and Territorial Gross Domestic Product by Income and by Expenditure Accounts
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 3.1, the DIVISION 1 interpretation section governing the all-provinces formula, adopts the accounts' definitions by name: 'household final consumption expenditures as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its Provincial and Territorial Economic Accounts, net of any taxes on products, also as determined by Statistics Canada', with the same 'for the purpose of its Provincial and Territorial Economic Accounts' construction pinning residential renovations, residential housing transfers and the housing expenditure categories to the same product. The Nova Scotia division uses it too, at s. 8(1)(z.2)-(z.4), e.g. 'household disposable income in the province ... as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its Provincial and Territorial Economic Accounts'. `calculated_from` because these are defined terms of the statutory payment formula, not background data.

rows.target_title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 3.1 (DIVISION 1) cites the tables down to the individual matrix: capital expenditures are 'expenditures on commodities, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its Provincial Supply and Use Tables' summary level final demand matrix' and intermediate input expenditures are 'expenditures on intermediate inputs, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of its Provincial Supply and Use Tables' summary level intermediate input matrix'. The Nova Scotia division draws GDP at factor cost from the same tables at s. 8(1)(z). Remapped from the handoff's proposed statcan-provincial-supply-use-tables node onto the existing statcan-sut node: both are IMDB record 1401 — the handoff itself cites record 1401 and table 36-10-0478-01, which is a record 1401 product — and the provincial tables are the provincial detail of that one programme, not a separate release.

rows.target_title: Canadian Government Finance Statistics (CGFS)
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 5(b)(ii), in the DIVISION 1 all-provinces business-income revenue base, computes 'the product, as determined on the basis of data prepared by Statistics Canada for the purpose of the Government Finance Statistics, of' the government business enterprise profit terms, and uses the same construction a second time in the same subparagraph ('the difference, as determined on the basis of data prepared by Statistics Canada for the purpose of the Government Finance Statistics'). The identical wording recurs in the Territorial Formula Financing part at s. 19(1)(b)(ii). `calculated_from` because the GFS data are operands of the statutory product, not context.

rows.target_title: Annual Oil and Gas Extraction Survey (OGEX)
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(m) through (s), the Nova Scotia division's oil and gas revenue bases, repeatedly pin production volumes and values to the survey by name — representative wording from s. 8(1)(p), mined oil revenues: 'the total value of the marketable production of synthetic petroleum from hydrocarbon deposits in the province in the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada on the basis of its survey Oil and Gas Extraction'. The survey also carries the statutory definitions of value of oil (s. 8(4)) and value of natural gas (s. 8(6)). Scope: DIVISION 2 (Nova Scotia additional-equalization calculation) only, not the live all-provinces formula.

rows.target_title: Sales of fuel used for road motor vehicles, annual (table 23-10-0066-01)
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 1(1), the general Interpretation section, defines the fuel quantities used across the instrument's motive-fuel tax bases against the table by its modern number: the 'adjusted number of litres of diesel fuel taxed at road-use rate' and 'adjusted number of litres of gasoline taxed at road-use rate' are each the quantities 'sold in the province or territory during the calendar year that ends in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of table 23-10-0066-01, Sales of fuel used for road motor vehicles, annual (x 1,000)'. Being a s. 1 definition, the citation applies wherever those defined terms are used in the Regulations.

rows.target_title: Value of sales of alcoholic beverages of liquor authorities and other retail outlets, by beverage type (table 10-10-0011-01)
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 19(1)(f) (Territorial Formula Financing) measures the alcohol revenue base against the modern table three times over: the volume of spirits, of wine and of beer 'sold in the province or territory in the fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of table 10-10-0011-01, Value of sales of alcoholic beverages of liquor authorities and other retail outlets, by beverage type (x 1,000)'. The Nova Scotia division cites the same product under its retired predecessor number at s. 8(1)(j), 'as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of CANSIM table 183-0024' — StatCan's own table page confirms 10-10-0011-01 was 'formerly CANSIM 183-0024', so both citations resolve to this node.

rows.target_title: Balance sheet of the agricultural sector as at December 31st (table 32-10-0056-01)
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(z), the Nova Scotia division's property-tax revenue base, takes 'the value of farm land in the province, measured in current dollars as of the end of the calendar year that ends in the preceding fiscal year, as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of CANSIM table 002-0020, Balance sheet of the agricultural sector, at December 31'. StatCan's table page confirms 32-10-0056-01 was 'formerly CANSIM 002-0020'. Scope: DIVISION 2 only — the Territorial Formula Financing parallel at s. 19(1)(h) measures farm value from the Census of Agriculture instead.

rows.target_title: Vehicle Registrations
rows.basis: SOR/2007-303 s. 8(1)(h) and (i), the Nova Scotia division's motor vehicle licensing revenue bases, count registered vehicles by category 'each as determined by Statistics Canada for the purpose of CANSIM table 405-0004, Road motor vehicles, registrations, or by the Minister if Statistics Canada does not make the determination'. The trailing clause is a statutory fallback for a discontinued source — the second such found in this corpus after the Oil Sands Royalty Regulation's Bank of Canada exchange-rate provision. The CANSIM number is retired; the producing programme is Statistics Canada's Vehicle Registrations programme, IMDB record 2747, which remains active. Scope: DIVISION 2 only.

rows.basis: Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act s. 24.1(1)(a)(v): for each fiscal year beginning after March 31, 2017 the cash contribution is the previous year's contribution multiplied by 'the greater of 1.03 and the amount determined by the formula (1 + A) where A is the average of the annual rates of growth of the nominal gross domestic product of Canada for the calendar year that ends during the fiscal year in question and for the two previous calendar years, as determined by the Minister not later than three months before the beginning of that fiscal year.' Section 2(3.1) names the source: 'the gross domestic product of Canada for a calendar year is the gross domestic product of Canada for the year as determined by the Chief Statistician of Canada in prescribed manner.' Finance Canada's public page states the same rule: 'Since 2017-18, total CHT funding has been legislated to grow in line with a three-year moving average of nominal gross domestic product (GDP), with total funding guaranteed to increase by at least 3 per cent per year.'

rows.target_title: Quarterly Demographic Estimates (Population estimates, quarterly)

Section 2 of the Canada Health Transfer, Canada Social Transfer and Wait Times Reduction Transfer Regulations then prescribes which series that is: 'For the purposes of these Regulations and Part V.1 of the Act, the manner in which the Chief Statistician of Canada shall determine the population of a province for a fiscal year is by basing that determination on Statistics Canada's official estimate of the population of the province on (a) June 1 of that fiscal year, for any fiscal year ending before April 1, 2024; or (b) July 1 of that fiscal year, for any fiscal year beginning after March 31, 2024.'

Section 2 of the CHT/CST Regulations prescribes that population as 'Statistics Canada's official estimate of the population of the province on ... July 1 of that fiscal year' for fiscal years beginning after March 31, 2024.

rows.basis: On 5 May 2020 PSAB approved 'Option 2 - Adapt IPSAS principles when developing future standards' as its International Strategy: PSAB continues to issue Canadian Public Sector Accounting Standards, but future standards are based on the principles in the corresponding IPSAS, and PSAB will only amend an IPSAS principle where it is contrary to PSAB's own Conceptual Framework. PSAB has separately proposed modifying the Canadian public sector GAAP hierarchy in Section PS 1150 to position IPSAS as the go-to framework where PSAB has not issued a specific standard.

The United Nations reviews and sets census recommendations and principles every 10 years to ensure international consistency.' It adds that under the revised Statistics Act 'the census will follow the highest international standards'. candidates.sentence: （ⅻ）その他の項目の推計方法 １．経済活動別就業者数・雇用者数・労働時間 （１）就業者数・雇用者数 就業者数・雇用者数は、主に『国勢統計』を用いて産業別、従業上の地位別（雇用 者、自営業主、家族従業者）に推計する。『国勢統計』実施年の９月分については同 調査を用いるが、それ以外の月は『労働力統計』を用いて月次ごとに推計する。なお、 国民経済計算では２つ以上の仕事に従事し、かつ事業所も異なる場合は、それぞれ一 人と数える（副業者分の概念）。このため、 『就業構造基本統計』 （総務省、５年ごと） を用い、就業者に占める副業者の割合から求める副業者比率によって副業者数を推 計し、就業者数に加算する。このようにして得た副業者を含む産業別、従業上の地位 別の就業者を『経済構造実態調査』 、『経済センサス-活動調査』等を用い、経済活動 別に分割する。年及び四半期値については、月次の値のそれぞれ 12 か月、３か月の 平均値とする。

candidates.sentence: （ⅻ）その他の項目の推計方法 １．経済活動別就業者数・雇用者数・労働時間 （１）就業者数・雇用者数 就業者数・雇用者数は、主に『国勢統計』を用いて産業別、従業上の地位別（雇用 者、自営業主、家族従業者）に推計する。『国勢統計』実施年の９月分については同 調査を用いるが、それ以外の月は『労働力統計』を用いて月次ごとに推計する。なお、 国民経済計算では２つ以上の仕事に従事し、かつ事業所も異なる場合は、それぞれ一 人と数える（副業者分の概念）。このため、 『就業構造基本統計』 （総務省、５年ごと） を用い、就業者に占める副業者の割合から求める副業者比率によって副業者数を推 計し、就業者数に加算する。このようにして得た副業者を含む産業別、従業上の地位 別の就業者を『経済構造実態調査』 、『経済センサス-活動調査』等を用い、経済活動 別に分割する。年及び四半期値については、月次の値のそれぞれ 12 か月、３か月の 平均値とする。
candidates.why: names artefact (cjk:国民経済計算) · dependency phrase

candidates.sentence: 例えば、サーバのヘドニック回帰式（2000年基準企業物価指数 （CGPI）の参考資料「 ヘドニック法の適用実績（汎用コンピュータ・サーバ＜うち、サーバ＞） 」）では、「CPUクロック周波数」、「最大キャッシュメモリ容量」、「最大搭載ハードディスク容量」、「最大搭載メモリ容量」、等がサーバの特性として用いられています。このような特性を変数とするヘドニック回帰式を推計し、推計された回帰式を用いて、諸特性の変化による「品質変化に見合う価格変化」を定量的に把握し、品質調整を行っております。なお、2005年6月公表の再推計では、性能に応じて用途やユーザー、価格帯が大きく異なることから、CPUの最大搭載個数4個以上の機種（上位機種）と2個以下の機種（下位機種）に分けて推計を行っています。

candidates.sentence: 企業物価指数は、統計法第8条に基づき、総務大臣に届出を行ったうえで実施している「届出統計調査」の1つであり、届出た書面によって毎月行っています。具体的には、毎月中旬に所定の「価格調査表」（2000年基準企業物価指数 （CGPI）の関連資料「 価格調査表の雛型 」参照）を価格調査先に送付し、予め特定された商品のその月における代表的な取引価格を記入していただいたうえで、翌月初に回収しています。その際、価格調査先に対しては、その月に契約が行われた主要取引先への販売価格をご報告いただくことを原則として依頼しています。回収された「価格調査表」（調査価格）は、調査統計局物価統計担当部署の約20名の担当者によって精査されたうえで集計システムに入力され、企業物価指数が作成されます。作成された指数は、速報は翌月の、確報は翌々月の第8営業日（定例的な遡及結果が反映される4月、10月の公表日は第9営業日）の午前8時50分に対外公表することを原則としています。なお、最新データの公表時間などについては、 項目2-39 および 2-40 をご覧ください。
candidates.why: names artefact (cjk:企業物価指数) · dependency phrase · carries a year

rows.target_title: Loi organique N°05-001/AU du 16 janvier 2005 fixant la quote-part des recettes publiques à partager entre l'Union et les Îles Autonomes
rows.basis: km-loi-finances-2026's own description already quotes the 2016 Loi de Finances (Article 8), which names 'la loi organique portant fixation des quotes-parts' as the legal basis for the residual-revenue split and gives the percentages 'Union / 37,5%... Nqazidja [Ngazidja] / 27,4%... Ndzouani / 25,7%... Mwali / 9,4%'. Those four figures match this organic law's Article 8 formula exactly (Union 37,50% / Ngazidja 27,4% / Anjouan 25,7% / Mohéli 9,4%), and Article 7 of the organic law states the mechanism 'ne peut être modifié que par une loi organique' (can only be amended by [another] organic law) -- i.e. the annual finance law's residual-split percentages are calculated per this organic law's formula, not independently set each year. Note this is distinct from the separate 1,85%-of-internal-revenue 'gouvernorats' pooled-transfer mechanism in the 2026 edition's own Article 4, which is a different, smaller allocation than the Article 8 residual-quote-part split.

rows.target_title: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP)
rows.basis: Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: STATEC 'établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés' [establishes monthly a consumer price index in accordance with the provisions of Council Regulation (EC) No 2494/95 of 23 October 1995 on harmonised indices of consumer prices]. Same shape as de-destatis-national-accounts -> esa-2010: a binding EU regulation supplies the definitions and methodology a national release conforms to, not figures. eurostat-hicp's own description states it is 'calculated according to a harmonised approach and definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations' -- the same regulatory framework named here. Not extended to lu-statec-ipcn: Art. 1er says the IPCN merely 'se conforme aux mêmes principes et concepts méthodologiques' [conforms to the same methodological principles and concepts] as the IPCH, without itself being subject to Regulation 2494/95 -- a Research.1 §5a 'comparable with' shape, not a documented dependency, so no edge is drawn for the IPCN side.

rows.target_title: CRA payroll deduction (PD7) accounts
rows.basis: Record 2612, Data sources: 'The statistics compiled by SEPH are based on a census of administrative records for all in-scope establishments with employees that can be found on the Business Register. Administrative information for total gross monthly payrolls and the total number of employees for the last pay period in the month are obtained from payroll deduction (PD7 form) accounts maintained by Canada Revenue Agency.' A census of these records rather than a sample of employers, which makes this the strongest available characterisation short of calculated_from. Held at uses_data_from because SEPH applies estimation on top — the same record describes model groups and a Business Payrolls Survey filling gaps — so the payroll figure is not arithmetic on the remittances alone.

rows.target_title: Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (MSM)
rows.basis: IMDB record 1301, the monthly GDP-by-industry programme, states its indicator sources by name: 'Data from the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing are used as indicators for most manufacturing industries. Data from the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours are used for many service industries.' The same sentence is the basis for the already-existing edge to statcan-seph, so `uses_data_from` follows that precedent. Corroborated independently by the programme's own source table, which names 'Monthly Survey of Manufacturing, Record no. 2101' in the gross-output rows for manufacturing industries — the same table and the same rows that produced the IPPI edge in V0.11.

rows.target_title: Annual Survey of Manufacturing and Logging Industries (ASML)
rows.basis: Stated by the annual survey rather than by the monthly one, in the present tense. IMDB record 2103: 'Within Statistics Canada, the data are used by the Canadian System of National Accounts, the Monthly Survey of Manufacturing (record number 2101) and Prices programs.' This is a reverse-direction disclosure — the target naming its consumers — and it is the only present-tense statement available. Record 2101's own account of the relationship is past tense and expired: 'Up to and including 2003, the MSM was benchmarked to the Annual Survey of Manufactures and Logging (ASML)', which is recorded in the `_dropped` block rather than used here, because a benchmarking arrangement that ended in 2003 is not a live dependency.

Under the NAICS, logging establishments are classified to NAICS code 1133 and manufacturing establishments to NAICS sectors 31, 32 and 33.' Restated in the sampling description: 'Prior to the selection of a random sample, enterprises are classified into homogeneous groups (i.e., groups with the same North American Industry Classification System codes and same geography) based on the characteristics of their establishments.'

rows.target_title: National Occupational Classification (NOC) 2021 Version 1.0
rows.basis: THE WEAKEST EDGE IN THIS SLICE, and flagged rather than buried. The NOC 2021 introduction states: 'It is important to note that the redesign of the NOC can have significant implications for several Surveys, such as the Labour Force Survey (LFS), and ESDC programs such as the Temporary Foreign Worker Program and Employment Insurance program.' This is a statement that a revision reaches the LFS, not a statement that the LFS uses the NOC, and the direction has to be read out of it rather than off it. It is taken on the precedent already set for boc-prime-rate -> boc-policy-rate, which rests on the Bank of Canada's word 'affects' and was accepted as `uses_data_from` on exactly that reasoning. It is also corroborated structurally by NOC being 'the departmental standard for data collection and dissemination for occupations at Statistics Canada' as of 10 August 2021. The clean version of this edge is a passage in the LFS's own record 3701 saying it codes occupation to NOC; that passage has not been retrieved, and the `_dropped` block records it as the lead to close.

rows.target_title: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992
rows.basis: Local Authorities Act 23 of 1992, s.77(1)-(2): 'There shall be levied for the benefit of the funds of regional councils an amount equal to five per cent of the rates levied under section 73 on all rateable property situated in local authority areas. ... The amount referred to in subsection (1) shall be collected by a local authority council situated in the region of the regional council concerned ... and paid over to the regional council.' A regional council's funds under Regional Councils Act s.33(1)(a) ('moneys appropriated by law for purposes of the funds of the regional council') include this amount, which is mechanically computed as a fixed 5% of the local-authority property rates levied under the Local Authorities Act s.73 -- the clearest documented municipal-to-regional fiscal-transfer formula found in this round's research.

rows.target_title: Local Government Act 2002
rows.basis: The class node's own defining statute. LGA 2002 s.98 requires every local authority to prepare an annual report; Schedule 10 Part 3 sets its required content -- clause 29 requires audited financial statements, clause 30A requires 'the number of rating units within the district or region of the local authority at the end of the preceding financial year' and total capital and land values. Already the basis for this node's own description before nz-lga-2002 existed as a node to point at.

rows.target_title: Property Assessment Notice and Assessment Roll (Current Value Assessment)
rows.basis: 2026 OMPF Technical Guide, Appendix F 'Data sources', which names MPAC in three of its twelve rows: 'Weighted Assessment | 2025 Returned Roll and 2026 starting tax ratios | Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) and municipal tax rate bylaws'; 'Number of Households | 2025 | MPAC (Municipal Property Assessment Corporation) Returned Roll'; and 'Farm Land Area | 2024 | MPAC (Municipal Property Assessment Corporation) and Ontario Parcel'. The guide body states the dependency again in prose for the farm measure: the land 'must be assessed and valued as farm land by the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC)'. This is a named organisation *and* a named product — the Returned Roll — which is what distinguishes it from the five agency-only Statistics Canada rows in the same table that were declined. Weighted Assessment per Household is also the primary indicator in the Municipal Fiscal Circumstances Index, so this is not a peripheral input: it is the measure the allocation turns on.

rows.target_title: Census of Population
rows.basis: NARROW, AND THE NARROWNESS IS THE FINDING. Appendix F attributes six separate indicators to 'Statistics Canada' and names no release for any of them, which is agency-level attribution and the same test that removed `boc-mpr -> statcan-national-accounts` in V0.9 and killed the H.15 restoration in V0.10. Five of the six are therefore declined and recorded in _dropped. Exactly one names a publication, in Appendix G's definition of the Rural and Small Community Measure: 'The measure is based on Statistics Canada data from the 2021 Census.' That is a named recurring release and it carries this edge, alone. The basis is written this way because the edge would otherwise be read as covering all six, and a later pass finding the other five undocumented would think this edge had been demoted rather than that it had always been this narrow. STRUCTURAL NOTE: this single sentence is also the only documented link between Ontario and the rest of the corpus. Without it the two nodes in this slice would form a second connected component, breaking an invariant held since V0.8. The graph stays at one component on the strength of one clause in an appendix definition.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index
rows.basis: The archived 2023-2025 version of the 'Indexing of Benefits' policy in the Alberta AISH policy manual (retained on the current Benefit Rate Adjustments page) states: 'AISH benefits are adjusted annually using the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) starting on January 1, 2023 ... Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the Alberta CPI (All-items, not seasonally adjusted). The Alberta CPI is published monthly by Statistics Canada and measures the change in price for goods and services bought by Albertans.' It sets out the formula X = A/B - 1, where A is the sum of the monthly Alberta CPI indexes for the 12 months ending September 30 before the adjustment date and B is the sum for the preceding 12 months. From January 1, 2026 the dependence on Alberta CPI is mediated by the Alberta escalator, which is capped at 2%.

rows.target_title: Alberta Escalator (Alberta Personal Income Tax Act indexation factor)
rows.basis: The current 'Benefit Rate Adjustments' policy (last updated July 2, 2026) in the Disability Income Assistance Policy Manual states: 'AISH and ADAP benefit rates are adjusted annually, effective January 1st of each year. Starting January 1, 2026, the rate of adjustment is based on the standard escalator amount established under section 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act.' It adds: 'Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the standard escalator amount established in the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, which is the lesser of either two per cent, or the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) amount from October through September year-over-year.' The policy cites as authority the AISH Act s. 3.1(2), the AISH General Regulations s. 7(3) and the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act s. 44.2. Living allowance, the modified living allowance personal allowance, the child benefit and most personal benefits are adjusted; health benefits and actual-cost benefits are not.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index
rows.basis: Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, RSA 2000 c A-30, s. 44.2(0.1)(b) defines the Alberta escalator, absent a prescribed percentage, as the lesser of 2% and the amount determined by the formula A/B - 1, 'where A is the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for the 12-month period that ended on the last September 30 before that year, and B is the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for the 12-month period immediately preceding'. Subsection 44.2(3) then defines that index explicitly: 'the Consumer Price Index for Alberta for any 12-month period is the result arrived at by (a) aggregating the Consumer Price Index for Alberta, as published by Statistics Canada under the authority of the Statistics Act (Canada) ... for each month in that period, (b) dividing the aggregate ... by 12'.

rows.target_title: Alberta Escalator (Alberta Personal Income Tax Act indexation factor)
rows.basis: Alberta Personal Income Tax Act, RSA 2000 c A-30, s. 44.2(2): 'Where the base taxation year ... in relation to a particular month is after 2024, each of the amounts expressed in dollars in section 30.2(2), except the amount of $2760, is to be adjusted so that the amount to be used under that subsection for the month is the total of (a) the amount that would, but for subsection (4), be the amount used under section 30.2(2) for the month that is one year before the particular month, and (b) the product obtained by multiplying (i) the amount referred to in clause (a) by (ii) the Alberta escalator for the taxation year following the base taxation year.' Section 30.2(2) is the Alberta Child and Family Benefit formula, containing the per-child base and working component amounts and the net income phase-out thresholds. The $2,760 working-income entry threshold is expressly excluded from indexation.

rows.target_title: Old Age Security Payment Indexation
rows.basis: The Seniors Benefit Act (RSA 2000 c S-7) Schedule puts federal OAS and GIS amounts directly inside the Alberta formulas. Schedule s. 9(2)(b)(ii) sets the special needs component income test as 'the sum of (A) the single senior non-deductible income amount under section 8 for the benefit adjustment year, plus (B) an amount equal to the maximum annual amount, not including retroactive payments and not adjusted for deferral, of the monthly pension payable to a single senior under the Old Age Security Act (Canada) in the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.' Schedule s. 7(4) defines term C of the supplementary accommodation assistance formula as 'the combined maximum annual amount ... of Old Age Security, not adjusted for deferral, and Guaranteed Income Supplement payable to a single senior and the maximum benefit payable to a single senior under section 4, in the previous calendar year.' The programme page corroborates that receipt of OAS is an eligibility condition and that lines 11300 (OAS) and 14600 (net federal supplements: GIS and Allowance) are deducted in arriving at non-deductible income (https://www.alberta.ca/alberta-seniors-benefit).

rows.target_title: Canada Pension Plan annual benefit adjustment (Pension Index)
rows.basis: Seniors Benefit Act Schedule, s. 8: '(1) The non-deductible income amount is (a) $23 020 for single seniors, and (b) $34 460 for senior couples. (2) Effective the benefit adjustment date of each benefit adjustment year, the non-deductible income amount is the non-deductible income amount in the previous benefit adjustment year increased annually by a percentage equivalent to the Pension Index under the Canada Pension Plan (Canada) that was applicable for the calendar year that ended before the commencement of the benefit adjustment year.' Subsection (3) adds a fallback: the Minister, in consultation with the Minister responsible for the Financial Administration Act, determines the adjustment 'if (a) the method of calculating the Pension Index is modified by the Government of Canada, or (b) the change in the Pension Index cannot be determined for any reason.' This is a rare case of an Alberta benefit threshold being escalated by a federal index rather than the Alberta escalator.

rows.target_title: Alberta Escalator (Alberta Personal Income Tax Act indexation factor)
rows.basis: The 'Benefit Rate Adjustments' policy in the Income and Employment Supports Policy Manual cites as authority the Income and Employment Supports Act s. 1(a.01), the Income Support, Training and Health Benefits Regulation s. 24.2, and the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act s. 44.2, and states: 'Income Support benefit rates are adjusted annually, effective January 1st of each year. Starting January 1, 2026, the rate of adjustment is based on the standard escalator amount established under section 44.2 of the Alberta Personal Income Tax Act.' It specifies that the adjusted core benefits are 'Core essential payment including the comforts allowance' and 'Core shelter payment', and that supplementary benefits are adjusted except where they are actual-cost, set by agreement, or set in separate legislation.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index
rows.basis: The archived 2023-2025 version of the same 'Benefit Rate Adjustments' / 'Indexing of Benefits' policy, retained on the page, states: 'Income Support benefits are adjusted annually using the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) starting on January 1, 2023 ... Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the Alberta CPI (All-items, not seasonally adjusted). The Alberta CPI is published monthly by Statistics Canada'. It gives the same X = A/B - 1 formula over 12-month periods ending September 30, and notes that 'Benefits are not adjusted in a year where the change in the Alberta CPI is a negative number'. From 2026 the CPI link runs through the Alberta escalator's 2% cap.

candidates.sentence: How Benefits are Indexed Annual benefit rate changes are calculated using the standard escalator amount established in the Alberta Personal Income Tax Ac t, which is the lesser of either two per cent, or the Alberta Consumer Price Index (CPI) amount from October through September year-over-year.

rows.target_title: Continuing Care Resident Accommodation Charges (maximum charges, types A and B)
rows.basis: The AISH/ADAP 'Benefit Rate Adjustments' policy carves the accommodation component of the modified living allowance out of the escalator and points it at the continuing care regulation instead: the adjusted core benefits are the living allowance and the 'Personal allowance of the modified living allowance', with the note 'Accommodation rates are adjusted separately in accordance with section 11(1)(2) of the Continuing Care (Ministerial) Regulation.' The AISH Financial Benefits Summary makes the same point about the modified living allowance: 'The accommodation room rate charges are established under the Continuing Care Act.' The Alberta Health accommodation charges page confirms it is the government that 'sets the maximum resident accommodation charge in type A and type B continuing care homes'.

rows.target_title: Continuing Care Resident Accommodation Charges (maximum charges, types A and B)
rows.basis: The Income Support 'Benefit Rate Adjustments' policy states: 'For client household units living in a Type A or Type B continuing care home, the accommodation rates are adjusted separately in accordance with section 11(1)(2) of the Continuing Care (Ministerial) Regulation.' The accommodation component of an Income Support client's benefit therefore tracks the Alberta Health maximum accommodation charge table rather than the Alberta escalator.

rows.target_title: Continuing Care Resident Accommodation Charges (maximum charges, types A and B)
rows.basis: Seniors Benefit Act Schedule, s. 7(4) makes the continuing care charge a literal term in the formula: the maximum supplementary accommodation assistance component is adjusted annually 'by an amount determined by the following formula: X = A + B - (C/12) where ... A is the maximum monthly accommodation charge set under the Continuing Care Act in respect of a private room that is in effect on the first day of the month after the accommodation adjustment date; B is the monthly disposable income amount added to the maximum monthly accommodation charge under subsection (2)(a)'. The programme page restates this in plain language - the Supplementary Accommodation Benefit is determined by 'the maximum monthly accommodation charge for a private room in a continuing care home' and 'the monthly disposable income amount of at least $373' - and the Alberta Health charges page confirms it from the other side: 'accommodation charges may be fully or partly covered for low-income residents who are either eligible for the Alberta Seniors Benefit [or] clients of the Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH) program ... residents who are eligible for benefits through these programs will be assured of at least $373 per month in disposable income after their monthly accommodation charge is paid.'

rows.target_title: CPP Disability Benefit Amount
rows.basis: The Disability Income Assistance Policy Manual 'Pension Income' policy (authority: AISH Act s. 3.2; AISH General Regulation s. 2.01(1)(c) and Schedule 1) lists 'CPP Disability' among the pension income sources and states: 'Applicants and clients pension income is non-exempt and deducted dollar for dollar as this type of income is intended to cover basic living needs, similar to AISH and ADAP.' It also states the interaction at the margin: 'If clients' Canada Pension Plan - Disability benefits increase to the point where they are no longer eligible for the AISH or ADAP monthly living allowance, they will continue to receive the same health coverage they had on AISH or ADAP through the Alberta Adult Health Benefit (AAHB) program.' The CPP-D amount is therefore a direct, dollar-for-dollar input to the AISH/ADAP payment calculation.

rows.target_title: Old Age Security Payment Indexation
rows.basis: The same 'Pension Income' policy lists 'Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS)', 'Old Age Security', 'Old Age Security Allowance (spouse)' and 'Old Age Security Supplement (survivor)' as pension income, and then makes federal OAS/GIS receipt a hard eligibility bar: 'Applicants and clients receiving the following pension income(s) are not eligible to receive AISH or ADAP: Alberta Seniors Benefits (except for where the applicant or client is 65 years old or older and they have not lived in Canada long enough to receive Old Age Security); Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS); or Old Age Security.' Where it is not disqualifying, pension income is 'non-exempt and deducted dollar for dollar'.

rows.target_title: Alberta Seniors Benefit maximum benefit amounts, income thresholds and phase-out rates
rows.basis: The 'Pension Income' policy lists 'Alberta Seniors Benefits' as a source of pension income for AISH/ADAP purposes, and names it first among the 'Pension Income Types That Cause AISH and ADAP Ineligibility': 'Applicants and clients receiving the following pension income(s) are not eligible to receive AISH or ADAP: Alberta Seniors Benefits (except for where the applicant or client is 65 years old or older and they have not lived in Canada long enough to receive Old Age Security)'. Receipt of the Alberta Seniors Benefit is thus an input to AISH/ADAP eligibility determination.

rows.target_title: CPP Disability Benefit Amount
rows.basis: The Disability Income Assistance Policy Manual's 'Alberta Adult Health Benefit' policy (authority: Income and Employment Supports Act, Part 2, Division 2; Income Supports, Training and Health Benefits Regulation ss. 73-90) states: 'The Alberta Adult Health Benefit (AAHB) program provides health benefits to clients who no longer qualify for AISH or ADAP due to income from: Employment or self-employment income of a cohabiting partner; The Canada Pension Plan Disability (CPP-D) program; or a combination of these and other types of income that are not exempt through AISH or ADAP.' CPP-D is named explicitly as one of the three income sources that route a person into AAHB, so the federal CPP-D amount determines who falls under the AAHB qualifying income levels.

rows.target_title: AISH/ADAP Financial Benefits Summary (benefit rate schedule)
rows.basis: The AAHB policy in the Disability Income Assistance Policy Manual states its purpose as 'To assist eligible former AISH and ADAP clients to maintain health benefits when they no longer qualify for AISH or ADAP', and describes the handover mechanically: 'When an AISH or ADAP client enrols in the AAHB program, health coverage transitions from AISH or ADAP to the AAHB program without interruption.' Entry to AAHB is triggered by the AISH/ADAP income test - that is, by the AISH exemption thresholds and living allowance in the AISH benefit rate schedule - and clients can return to AISH or ADAP from AAHB without a new application in most circumstances.

rows.target_title: AISH/ADAP Financial Benefits Summary (benefit rate schedule)
rows.basis: The AADL cost-sharing page states that 'client[s] pay 25% of the cost of program benefits up to a maximum of $500 per family per benefit year (July 1 to June 30)' and that 'Clients receiving income supplement benefits from the following Alberta government programs may be exempt from cost-sharing: Income Support Program benefits; Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH); Alberta Adult Health Benefits (AAHB); Child and Youth Support Program; Children and Family Services (minors in foster care).' Enrolment in AISH (or Income Support, or AAHB) is therefore a direct input to whether a client owes the AADL cost-share; the page also instructs clients to contact AADL if they receive AISH or Alberta Works health benefits. The alternative test is a taxable income threshold on line 26000 of the most recent income tax return.

rows.target_title: Alberta Budget — Fiscal Plan
rows.basis: The 2026-29 Fiscal Plan (Budget 2026) is where the new disability assistance rate structure is set out: 'On July 1, 2026, the new Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP) will start ... The maximum ADAP benefit rate will be set at $1,740 per month. Clients who transition from AISH to ADAP will receive a transition benefit of $200 per month, maintaining the maximum total benefit at the same level as AISH until December 31, 2027. As with AISH, ADAP benefit rates will be subject to the Alberta escalator policy annually, and former ADAP clients will continue to receive ongoing health benefits until age 65, regardless of employment income.' The Budget therefore sets the starting level that the escalator subsequently indexes.

rows.target_title: Alberta Budget — Fiscal Plan
rows.basis: The 2026-29 Fiscal Plan sets the Alberta Seniors Benefit income thresholds directly: 'Effective July 1, 2026, the start of the 2026-27 benefit year, seniors' income thresholds for the Alberta Seniors Benefit will be reduced by 9 per cent, along with corresponding reductions for Special Needs Assistance for Seniors, and the grant component of the Seniors Home Adaptation and Repair Program thresholds, resulting in estimated savings of $23 million in 2026-27 and $31 million in 2027-28 and beyond.' A discretionary Budget decision can therefore override the statutory escalator in either direction for this programme.

rows.target_title: Alberta Budget — Fiscal Plan
rows.basis: The 2026-29 Fiscal Plan carries the 'Alberta Child and Family Benefit Program Parameters' table in its Tax Plan chapter, footnoted: 'Benefit amounts and phase-out thresholds have increased by 2% from 2025 due to the Alberta escalator.' The expense chapter explains the same movement in dollar terms: 'The Alberta Child and Family Benefit is budgeted at $405 million in 2026-27, an increase of $30 million, or 8 per cent from 2025-26 reflecting population growth, a 2 per cent escalator to benefit rates, and higher phase-out income thresholds.' The Budget is where the year's ACFB parameter table is authoritatively published.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index
rows.basis: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (browser session, closing the item G.64.md left as cheap check 1). Continuing Care (Ministerial) Regulation, Alta Reg 44/2024 under the Continuing Care Act, SA 2022, c C-26.7 -- office consolidation with amendments up to and including AR 199/2025, current as of August 27, 2025, fetched in full via a Chrome browser session (a direct fetch-tool request to the same PDF URL returns ROBOTS_DISALLOWED; the King's Printer PDF itself carries no such restriction against ordinary browser access). Section 11 in full: '11(1) In this section, “Alberta CPI” means the monthly All-items Consumer Price Index for Alberta, not seasonally adjusted, published by Statistics Canada. (2) The maximum amount of the accommodation charge set by the Minister under section 9(4) of the Act in respect of each type of accommodation must be adjusted annually on August 1 by the lesser of the following: (a) the percentage increase in the Alberta CPI for the 12-month period ending on February 28 of that year, rounded to the nearest $0.05; (b) 3.8%.' This both settles the edge and explains the number on Alberta Health's programme page: the 1.8% increase stated to take effect August 1, 2026 is the CPI figure under (a), sitting below the 3.8% cap under (b) and so the binding term. Note the reference window is 12 months ending February 28, not September 30 as in the other Alberta-CPI edges in this slice -- this regulation runs its own, differently-dated formula.

rows.target_title: Policy Interest Rate Announcement
rows.basis: Pure arithmetic on the target. The Bank's explainer works the example: 'if the Bank sets the policy interest rate at 2.25% ... the lower end of the range is 2.20%—our deposit rate; the higher end of the range is 2.5%—our bank rate.' The offsets are policy choices that change rarely — the deposit rate moved from equal to the target to 5 basis points below it in January 2025 — but between such changes the band is a fixed spread and nothing else.

rows.target_title: Policy Interest Rate Announcement
rows.basis: The Bank names this transmission directly: the policy rate 'is the starting point for setting many of the interest rates in the economy that matter for Canadians', and 'by encouraging financial institutions to borrow and lend among themselves at close to the policy rate, the Bank affects interest rates on all kinds of other borrowing in the economy, including the prime rate of commercial banks (used for loans such as mortgages and lines of credit)'. Deliberately not calculated_from: no bank is obliged to move prime, and the Bank's own word is 'affects'. The spread has been stable for years by convention, not by rule.

The 6% maximum operating reserve limit the division is tested against, and the grant rates its revenue is built from, both come from the manual — the budget notes ongoing deficits caused by 'rising operational costs ... without corresponding increases in grant rates'.

rows.target_title: Постановление Правительства РФ от 22.11.2004 N 670 (ред. от 15.12.2025) «О распределении дотаций на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности субъектов Российской Федерации» (Government of the Russian Federation Resolution No. 670 of 22.11.2004, as amended through 15.12.2025, "On the distribution of equalization grants for the budgetary sufficiency of constituent entities of the Russian Federation", together with the Methodology for distributing them)
rows.basis: Minted on a temporal-and-subject convergence, stated plainly so a reader can judge it, rather than on any single sentence declaring the link. Постановление N 670 is currently in force 'ред. от 15.12.2025' — i.e., its text as amended effective 15.12.2025, the amendment Budget Code Art. 131's own editorial note names as governing '2026 г.' grant distribution. The Ministry of Finance's 'Уровень расчетной бюджетной обеспеченности ... на 2026 год' document is dated/published on that exact same day, 15.12.2025, and concerns exactly the subject that instrument's title describes — the distribution of дотации на выравнивание бюджетной обеспеченности. Two independently primary/near-primary Russian government sources (a ConsultantPlus-mirrored resolution page and a minfin.gov.ru-hosted publication) converge on the same date and the same mechanism. `cites` rather than `calculated_from`/`methodology_depends_on`, deliberately the most conservative of the four relationship types available: no document text says in so many words that the Minfin table was produced by applying Resolution 670's formula, and that formula itself was never independently read (see `_dropped`), so the edge records the documented convergence rather than an unverified computational claim.

rows.basis: The monthly programme's industry-by-industry source table, 'National monthly gross domestic product by industry, summary of Methods and data sources' (2021), names the IPPI by title and by IMDB record number in 64 separate rows. Representative row, NAICS 3111 Animal food manufacturing, under 'Gross output': 'Sales and inventory change in constant prices, Monthly Survey of Manufacturing, Record no (number). 2101. Industrial product price indexes, Record no (number). 2318.' Record 2318 is the IPPI. `uses_data_from` follows the type already taken for statcan-gdp-monthly -> statcan-cpi, which rests on the identical evidence in the identical document. WORTH STATING PLAINLY: this is the best-evidenced deflator edge in the Canadian corpus and it was the last one built. The same table names the CPI in 27 rows and SEPH in 37, and both of those became edges two sessions before this one — the IPPI was invisible only because nobody had grepped for it. rows.target_title: Industrial Product Price Index (IPPI)
rows.basis: Catalogue 15F0077GIE, 'A Guide to Deflating the Input-Output Accounts: Sources and Methods' (2001), which record 1301 cites as the description of the double-deflation method used to produce constant-price GDP by industry. Under the heading 'Sources of deflators', unhedged: 'The main data source of deflators for manufactured goods is the Industrial Product Price Indexes (IPPI) produced by Statistics Canada's Prices Division. Prior to 1981, deflators were based on Industry Selling Price Indexes (ISPI).' Earlier in the same chapter, on why basic-price deflation is possible where purchaser-price deflation is not: 'the commodity price information collected by the Prices Division to compile industry product price indexes can be used to construct deflators for values at basic prices. These Industrial Product Price Indexes (IPPI), aggregated where necessary to the input-output classification, constitute the main source of deflators for manufactured commodities.' Both passages verified verbatim against the PDF. `methodology_depends_on` matches the type taken for statcan-sut -> statcan-cpi from the same document. ONE HEDGE, STATED, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE: the guide is a 2001 edition marked ARCHIVED, twenty-five years old, and it remains the document record 1301 points at for this method. The 'can be used' softness that qualifies the CPI edge does not apply here — the 'Sources of deflators' sentence says 'is'.

rows.target_title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
rows.basis: The reverse direction, and the graph's second mutual pair. Record 2318, under Estimation: 'For the IPPI, commodity and industry weights are derived from a combination of the 2019 Supply and Use Tables that closely reflect actual economic transactions by industry and the sales of goods manufactured by companies as reported for the 2019 ASML.' The same section adds that the industry indexes are 'aggregated to the level required for the input-output tables and the measurement of Gross Domestic Product', so the tables set the aggregation structure as well as the weights. Admissible under the V0.10 mutual-partner rule on its own terms: each direction is stated by a different document in its own words, each carries its own evidence_url, and the two are asymmetric in kind rather than restatements of one relationship — the tables take the IPPI as a price measure, the IPPI takes the tables as a weighting frame. `relationship_type` records the asymmetry as the rule requires: `methodology_depends_on` outbound from the tables against `uses_data_from` here, because the SUT figures are a direct numerical input to the weights rather than a method the IPPI follows. THE MECHANISM IS NOT SIMULTANEOUS AND THAT MATTERS FOR READING THE CYCLE: the 2019 tables weight today's index, and today's index deflates a later vintage of the tables. Nothing circular happens in any single calculation; the loop closes only across vintages, five years apart.

rows.target_title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
rows.basis: Record 1301 states the anchoring three separate ways in its own words. Under Estimation: 'The monthly estimates are benchmarked to annually chained Fisher volume indexes of GDP obtained from the constant-price supply and use tables.' Under Data accuracy: 'GDP by industry depends on the Supply and Use tables to which it is anchored', and 'as the monthly GDP by industry program relies on the annual estimates of real GDP obtained from the Supply and Use tables, the quality of these estimates has a direct influence on the quality of the monthly GDP measures.' Record 1401 says the same from the other side: 'two industry-based programs - one producing the country's current monthly GDP figures (record no. 1301), the other annual provincial-territorial estimates (record no. 1303) have been set up. These two programs, which can be viewed as extensions of the supply and use tables, use a set of indicators to project the GDP by industry benchmarks from the supply and use tables'. `calculated_from` because the monthly figure is literally a projection of a benchmark drawn from these tables, not merely informed by them — and note the release identifies the dependent by record number, which is the strongest cross-reference in the StatCan corpus so far.

rows.target_title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
rows.basis: Record 1901, under Estimation: 'The National Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by Income and by Expenditure Accounts are estimated by taking the most complete and high quality data sources available to establish annual benchmark estimates. ... The annual benchmarks for GDP by the income approach and by the expenditure approach are generated through the construction of annual supply and use tables which balance the supply of each product in the economy against its use. These tables present the most complete and accurate depiction of Canadian economic activity.' The same record's Revisions section adds that statistical revisions incorporate 'the annual benchmarking process of the supply and use tables'. This is the edge that makes the V0.10 deletion of statcan-national-accounts -> statcan-gdp-monthly legible rather than merely correct: the quarterly and monthly programmes do not read each other, they are two projections off this common annual benchmark.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index
rows.basis: Catalogue 15F0077GIE, 'A Guide to Deflating the Input-Output Accounts: Sources and Methods' (2001), which record 1301 cites as the description of the double-deflation method used to produce constant-price GDP by industry. Chapter 2, in the passage on trade margins: 'Consumer price indexes can be used to deflate the purchaser value of commodities sold for personal expenditure. Similarly, industry product price indexes are used to deflate the basic values of the same commodities. This has made it possible to calculate the trade margin for commodities bought for personal expenditure as a residual using both of these observed prices.' `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from` because this document is the accounts' deflation methodology and the index is named as the price measure the method takes, which is the case the type comment describes. ONE HEDGE REMAINS, AND ONE WAS RETIRED IN V0.11. Retired: the 'can be used' softness above is not the document's last word on the CPI. Four sentences later in the same passage, unhedged and read while verifying the IPPI quotations, the guide states the mechanism outright: 'The total trade margin at constant prices is calculated as the difference between the purchaser value, deflated with the appropriate Consumer Price Index (CPI), and the sum of the basic value and the ...'. 'Deflated with' is a statement of what deflates what, which is exactly what the hedged sentence was recorded as lacking, so this edge is stronger than V0.10 believed and was under-rated by a first reading that stopped at the first mention. Still standing: the guide is a 2001 edition marked ARCHIVED — it remains the document record 1301 points at for this method, but it is twenty-five years old and a later methodology note may supersede it.

rows.target_title: National Economic Accounts (Quarterly)
rows.basis: The reverse of statcan-national-accounts -> statcan-sut, and taken deliberately under the V0.10 decision that a node may be a mutual definitional partner. Record 1401, Quality evaluation: 'The input-output framework is validated for accuracy, coherence and overall reasonableness. The major components of the framework, such as the income and expenditure-based GDP components are reconciled to the national and provincial-territorial income and expenditure accounts.' Record 1901 states the converse in its own Estimation section: 'The annual benchmarks for GDP by the income approach and by the expenditure approach are generated through the construction of annual supply and use tables which balance the supply of each product in the economy against its use.' Neither statement is a mistake and neither supersedes the other — annual benchmarking is an iterative balancing process in which each side constrains the other, which is what the accounts mean by coherence. The pair is asymmetric in strength and the `relationship_type` records that: 1901 discloses the SUT as the source of its benchmark levels (`calculated_from`), while 1401 describes reconciliation as a validation step rather than an input (`methodology_depends_on`), so the cycle is not symmetric in weight and does not assert that the two are interchangeable.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (CPI-U / CPI-W)
rows.basis: SSA states the statutory formula outright: 'The Social Security Act specifies a formula for determining each COLA. According to the formula, COLAs are based on increases in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W). CPI-Ws are calculated on a monthly basis by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. A COLA effective for December of the current year is equal to the percentage increase (if any) in the CPI-W from the average for the third quarter of the current year to the average for the third quarter of the last year in which a COLA became effective.' The arithmetic is shown in full: the 2.8 percent COLA effective December 2025 is (317.265 - 308.729) / 308.729 x 100, using the July, August and September CPI-W values for 2024 and 2025. Note the index is CPI-W, a subpopulation index for urban wage earners and clerical workers, not the headline CPI-U.

rows.target_title: National Average Wage Index (AWI)
rows.basis: SSA lists the amounts driven by the wage index and puts the taxable maximum first: 'We use the average wage indexing series to update several amounts that are important to the operation of Social Security's Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program. — OASDI contribution and benefit base (also known as the taxable maximum); Retirement earnings test exempt amounts; Formulas for a primary insurance amount and maximum family benefits; Amount of earnings needed to earn a quarter of coverage.' This is the interesting structural fact about the Social Security system: benefits are indexed to prices, the tax base is indexed to wages, and the two indices diverge.

rows.target_title: Population Estimates Program (Vintage Estimates)
rows.basis: The Handbook of Methods is unambiguous that the survey cannot produce population levels by itself: 'Population controls are independent estimates of the population that are used to weight the CPS sample results so that estimates reflect the civilian noninstitutional population ages 16 and older. The Census Bureau develops the CPS population controls, which are based on decennial census population counts, supplemented with birth and death data and estimates of net international migration. The Census Bureau reviews and adjusts the population estimates every year. BLS introduces the Census Bureau's annual population control adjustments into CPS estimates for January.' This is why the January Employment Situation carries a break in the household series each year — the level jumps by whatever the new vintage says, independent of anything that happened in the labour market.

rows.target_title: Decennial Census of Population and Housing
rows.basis: The population controls are 'based on decennial census population counts, supplemented with birth and death data and estimates of net international migration' — the estimates programme is a carry-forward of the decennial base, which is why a census undercount or overcount propagates into every intercensal year until the next census resets it.

rows.target_title: Current Population Survey (CPS)
rows.basis: The Employment Situation news release is two surveys stapled together. The household half — the unemployment rate, the participation rate, and all demographic detail — is the CPS. BLS: 'When the Census Bureau's processing activities are completed, the microdata file is securely transferred to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) for estimation of labor force statistics.' The establishment half (payroll employment) is the CES, already linked to QCEW elsewhere in the graph.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (CPI-U / CPI-W)
rows.basis: The statute names the index: 'Section 673(2) of the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (OBRA) of 1981 (42 U.S.C. 9902(2)) requires the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services to update the poverty guidelines at least annually, adjusting them on the basis of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U). ... As required by law, this update is accomplished by increasing the latest published Census Bureau poverty thresholds by the applicable percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U). The guidelines in this 2026 notice reflect the 2.63 percent price increase between calendar years 2024 and 2025.' Note this is CPI-U, annual average to annual average — a different index and a different reference period from the CPI-W third-quarter comparison that drives the Social Security COLA.

The poverty guidelines continue to be derived from the Census Bureau's current official poverty thresholds; they are not derived from the Census Bureau's Supplemental Poverty Measure (SPM).'
