rows.basis: 'The official poverty thresholds do not vary geographically, but they are updated for inflation using the Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)... Thresholds are updated annually for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U).' Worth noting the doubling-up: the thresholds are CPI-indexed, and then HHS indexes the published thresholds forward by CPI again to get the guidelines, so the CPI enters the eligibility rule for Medicaid twice, a year apart.

rows.target_title: Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (C-CPI-U)
rows.basis: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 says the figures 'are generally determined by reference to § 1(f)', and 26 U.S.C. § 1(f) names the index and the reference period exactly: '(3)(A) The cost-of-living adjustment for any calendar year is the percentage (if any) by which (i) the C-CPI-U for the preceding calendar year, exceeds (ii) the CPI for calendar year 2016, multiplied by the amount determined under subparagraph (B).' '(6)(A) The term "C-CPI-U" means the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the Department of Labor). The values ... shall be the latest values so published as of the date on which such Bureau publishes the initial value of the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the month of August for the preceding calendar year.' '(6)(B) The C-CPI-U for any calendar year is the average of the C-CPI-U as of the close of the 12-month period ending on August 31 of such calendar year.' The August cut-off is why the IRS can publish next year's brackets in October, and the freeze on 'latest values as of' the initial August release is how the statute copes with the fact that the chained index is revised for a year after first publication.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (CPI-U / CPI-W)
rows.basis: The chained index is not a separate collection — it is the CPI's own price quotes reaggregated. BLS: 'all three of the CPI indexes are built in two stages. In the first stage, prices for each of the 7,776 item-area combinations (243 item categories X 32 geographic areas) are averaged together to form 7,776 basic indexes... The geometric mean estimator is used in the C-CPI-U in the same item categories in which it is used in the CPI-U and CPI-W. In the second stage... It is at this second stage where the C-CPI-U is different from the CPI-U and CPI-W. The use of a superlative formula for upper-level aggregation... is designed to address consumer substitution across item categories.' BLS also confirms the policy use: 'Since 2017, the C-CPI-U has been used to adjust Federal tax brackets for inflation.' The average gap is about 0.2 percentage points a year, which compounds.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (CPI-U / CPI-W)
rows.basis: NIPA Handbook Chapter 5 lists the CPI among the principal inputs — 'The following are among the principal source data used for the PCE estimates: BEA's Benchmark Input-Output (I-O) Accounts... the Census Bureau's Annual Retail Trade Survey, Service Annual Survey, Quarterly Services Survey, and Monthly Retail Trade Survey; and the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Consumer Price Indexes (CPIs)' — and then explains the mechanism: 'The estimates of quantities purchased, or real spending, for most of the detailed PCE categories are prepared by deflation. In this method, the quantities are calculated by dividing the current-dollar value of the component by an appropriate price index... For most PCE categories, the closest matching price index is a consumer price index or indexes.' Tables 5.A and 5.B name the specific CPI series component by component (CPI for new cars, CPI for used cars and trucks, CPI for food at home, and so on). The Fed's preferred inflation gauge is therefore largely a reweighting of BLS price quotes onto national-accounts expenditure weights.

rows.target_title: Personal Income and Outlays (incl. PCE Price Index)
rows.basis: The FOMC's Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, reaffirmed effective January 27, 2026, names the series that defines the target: 'The Committee reaffirms its judgment that inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent over the longer run with the Federal Reserve's statutory maximum employment and price stability mandates.' The 2 percent goal is not defined on the CPI — a distinction that matters because the two indexes routinely differ by several tenths.

rows.target_title: Personal Income and Outlays (incl. PCE Price Index)
rows.basis: The Summary of Economic Projections reports each participant's projection of inflation as the percent change in the PCE price index and in the core PCE price index, precisely because the FOMC's longer-run goal is stated as '2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures'. The projection variable is defined by the statement of goals, so the SEP inherits BEA's index by construction.

rows.basis: H.15's own footnotes 9 and 10 both read 'Source: U.S. Treasury' for the Treasury nominal and inflation-indexed constant maturity series, and the release describes those yields as 'interpolated by the U.S. Treasury from the daily yield curve'. rows.basis: The Handbook of Methods is explicit: 'The CPI uses data from the Consumer Expenditure (CE) survey to determine the weights of the different categories of goods and services in the CPI... Annual CE data are used for the CPI-U and CPI-W weights; these expenditure weights are updated annually.' The CE survey also selects the outlets where prices are collected. rows.target_title: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
rows.basis: The CES sampling frame 'is built from unemployment insurance (UI) quarterly tax records', and the net birth–death model that fills the gap left by firms too new to sample is derived from 'the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) universe employment series' via an ARIMA projection on ten years of QCEW history. rows.basis: ENCOVI reports directly on service failures (fallas de servicios de electricidad 7%, agua 5%) as one of its twelve survey items; independent 2026 coverage of ENCOVI 2025 confirms 'Acceso a servicios públicos' as a standing reported ENCOVI category.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (P0141)
rows.basis: Budget Review 2026, Chapter 5: 'The social grant allocation has been adjusted down over the medium term in line with a lower inflation outlook...' -- inflation is named as a factor in the allocation decision, but no formula ties the figure to a specific CPI print, so this is filed as `cites` (context) rather than `uses_data_from` (mechanical input). This absence of a formula is itself the finding, not an oversight in how the edge is drawn.

rows.target_title: Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004
rows.basis: SASSA Act s.3(a): the Agency's object is 'the efficient and effective management, administration and payment of social assistance' -- 'social assistance' being the scheme the Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004 establishes and defines. The two Acts were passed the same year and name two different things (a benefits scheme and the agency that pays it); this edge records the documented link between them rather than assuming one because of the similar names.

rows.target_title: South African Social Security Agency Act 9 of 2004
rows.basis: SASSA Act s.2(1) establishes SASSA as a juristic person; the Annual Report is the Agency's own statutory report on its performance and finances as that juristic person, so its existence depends directly on the Act that creates the Agency.

rows.target_title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Chapter 13 (Finance)
rows.basis: DoRA is the Act s.214(1)(a) requires Parliament to pass each year; its allocation is required to weigh the factors s.214(2) lists (basic-services capacity, fiscal capacity and efficiency, economic disparities). The Constitution supplies the criteria the annual Act's formula must apply, not a computed figure itself.

rows.target_title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Chapter 13 (Finance)
rows.basis: The framework names the local government equitable share (s.227(1)(a)) as the intended funding source for free basic services to the indigent, but states it is 'to be applied in conjunction with' equitable share policy rather than computed from a stated formula in this document -- filed as `cites`, same caution as the existing za-national-treasury-budget-review -> za-statssa-cpi edge.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (P0141)
rows.basis: SARB's own page: the inflation target 'refers to the headline change in the consumer price index, as calculated by Statistics South Africa' -- the repo-rate decision is defined directly in terms of Stats SA's CPI print, not merely informed by it. Same shape as the Bank of Canada / CPI edge already in the graph.

rows.target_title: Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP 2018)
rows.basis: Stats SA's own methodology report: 'The South African CPI adopted the 2018 version of the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP) for goods and services with effect from the January 2025 publication' -- COICOP 2018 structures the actual live basket, unlike the Canada/US cases where it was dropped for governing only a side series.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods
rows.basis: Stats SA's own methodology report: 'Stats SA largely follows the methodology guidelines of the 2020 Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods published jointly by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the International Labour Organization (ILO)...' -- the same `cpi-manual` node already in the graph (international-frameworks.json), now with a South African edge into it.

rows.target_title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)
rows.basis: Stats SA's own methodology report: 'The South African CPI complies with the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)' -- SDDS prescribes the release's coverage, periodicity, timeliness and advance-release-calendar practice, which is a dissemination-methodology obligation Stats SA states directly rather than one only asserted from the IMF side (the gap that got Canada's equivalent edge dropped).

rows.target_title: Estimates of National Expenditure (ENE) — Vote 19: Social Development
rows.basis: National Treasury's own language describes the Budget Review and the ENE as companion documents drawing on the same consolidated main-budget data, published together on Budget Day -- the ENE gives the vote-level detail (including Vote 19: Social Development) that the Budget Review discusses in aggregate. No stated formula computing one from the other, so filed as `cites` rather than `calculated_from` -- see _open_questions.

rows.target_title: Social Assistance Act 13 of 2004
rows.basis: Vote 19's own budget summary covers Social Assistance transfers and SASSA administration, ~99.6-99.7% of the vote's expenditure per the document itself -- the vote is the fiscal instrument funding the Act's grant system, though the vote document doesn't itself set grant amounts (that remains the Minister's Gazette-notice power under s.32(3), already in the graph).

rows.target_title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Schedule 4 (Functional Areas of Concurrent National and Provincial Legislative Competence)
rows.basis: The Annual Report's own text: 'Schedule 4 of the Constitution further identifies welfare services, population development and disaster management as functional areas of concurrent national and provincial legislative competence.'

rows.target_title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Schedule 4 (Functional Areas of Concurrent National and Provincial Legislative Competence)
rows.basis: The Western Cape APP lists the Constitution among its own governing mandates and operates under the same concurrent-competence framework for welfare services described in za-constitution-schedule4 -- it names s.28 (children's rights) alongside the concurrent listing rather than restating the Schedule 4 language verbatim itself, per the source describing it.

rows.target_title: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 — Chapter 13 (Finance)
rows.basis: Section 224 of the Constitution: 'The primary object of the South African Reserve Bank is to protect the value of the currency in the interest of balanced and sustainable economic growth in the Republic.' This resolves the open question left in za-fiscal-federalism.json about the SARB's statutory basis: the 3% (±1pp) numerical target itself is NOT written into the South African Reserve Bank Act 90 of 1989 (which only carries the older 'protect the value of the currency' language) -- it was set by a 2025 agreement between the Minister of Finance and the SARB Governor ('The Minister of Finance today announced a new inflation target for South Africa of 3% with a 1 percentage point tolerance band. This decision follows agreement between the Governor of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) and the Minister.'). A third South African mechanism, after grants (Gazette notice) and UIF (Gazette notice), that turns out to be discretionary/agreement-based rather than a hard statutory formula.

rows.target_title: Consumer Price Index (P0141)
rows.basis: The circular's macroeconomic table sources CPI Inflation forecasts to 'National Treasury Budget Review 2025,' and the companion circular states 'The Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation is forecasted to be 4.4 per cent' as the benchmark municipalities must justify against. Flagged as an indirect (Budget Review-mediated) rather than direct-quoted StatsSA link within the circular text itself.

rows.target_title: ICLS Resolution concerning statistics of work, employment and labour underutilization
rows.basis: The QLFS's own Q1 2026 technical notes: the questionnaire 'was revised in Q3: 2025 in order to adhere to the most recent international labour statistics standards', naming the 19th/20th/21st ICLS resolutions directly. Weaker than the equivalent statcan-lfs edge (see _open_questions) but real, national-side evidence of ICLS alignment.

rows.target_title: Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention, 1952 (No. 102)
rows.basis: s.12(3)(a): the Minister's Gazette-notice power to amend the UIF benefit scale is exercised 'in accordance with a maximum monthly rate of remuneration of a skilled manual labourer as determined by the Social Security (Minimum Standards) Convention' -- named as a reference benchmark for a discretionary power, not a formula the benefit is calculated from, and not a ratified treaty obligation. Filed as `cites` for both reasons.
